title: Status page + Console incident comms — UX copy WIP (titles, summaries, linking)
body:
Context
- Goal: tighten and standardize customer-facing microcopy for (a) public Status Page incident titles + updates, and (b) how we reference/link incidents + post-incident summaries from the Redwood Console.
- This is intentionally WIP. We should align with incident-bot templates + component taxonomy so the same terms show up everywhere.

Primary principles (copy + UX)
1) Be specific about the impacted surface (component + region + capability) without speculating on root cause.
2) Prefer “what customers experience” over internal system details.
3) Use consistent severity language, but avoid making an SLA promise.
4) If we don’t know something, say that clearly (and say what we’re doing next).
5) Don’t disclose customer-specific capacity, traffic patterns, or any single-tenant impact.
6) Don’t over-index on “everything is fine” if a subset is failing (avoid the “status says API ok but embeddings failing” problem).

Voice/tone guide
- Plain, direct, non-alarmist.
- Avoid overly technical phrasing (no internal service names, no shard/cluster details).
- Avoid absolutes: “fully resolved for all customers” unless verified.
- Avoid attributing fault to a provider/partner publicly.
- Use “some customers” only when we can bound impact by component/region and we’re confident it’s partial.

Terminology alignment (must match component taxonomy)
Use product/capability terms consistently:
- Hosted API: Chat/Completions (non-streaming)
- Streaming: streaming responses for chat/completions
- Embeddings
- Reranking
- Console
- Dedicated: Dedicated Control Plane (only if customer-facing; see Dedicated/Private guidance below)
- Regions: use standard labels (e.g., US East, US West, EU Central, APAC Singapore) — confirm exact display names with status page component registry.

Incident title patterns (Status Page)
Titles should be short, scannable, and consistent. Preferred format:
- "<Component> <issue type> in <Region>" or "<Component> <issue type> (<Region>)"

Issue type vocabulary (pick one)
- "Degraded performance" (latency elevated, partial failures, or timeouts)
- "Elevated error rates" (clear increase in 5xx/failed requests)
- "Partial outage" (material subset failing; not total)
- "Service outage" (majority failing; high confidence)
- "Delayed processing" (async jobs; only if applicable)

Examples (good)
- "Streaming degraded performance in US East"
- "Embeddings elevated error rates in EU Central"
- "Hosted API partial outage in US West"
- "Console degraded performance (Global)"

Examples (avoid)
- "API issues" (too vague)
- "Model outage" (ambiguous: which model? which surface?)
- "Kubernetes incident" (internal implementation detail)
- "GPU capacity problems" (sensitive; implies specific constraint + can be customer-specific)

Status Page update summary blocks (short + long)
Each update should have:
- 1st sentence: customer impact (what they see) + component/region
- 2nd sentence: what we’re doing now (investigating/mitigating/monitoring)
- Optional: workaround (only if safe + broadly applicable)
- Optional: next update timing (recommended for Sev0/Sev1)

Template microcopy (Status Page updates)

INVESTIGATING (initial)
Short (preferred):
- "We’re investigating elevated error rates affecting <Component> in <Region>. We’ll share updates as we learn more."

Slightly longer (if needed):
- "We’re investigating an issue affecting <Component> in <Region>. Some requests may fail or time out. We’ll provide an update within <X> minutes."

IDENTIFIED
- "We’ve identified the cause of elevated errors affecting <Component> in <Region> and are working on mitigation."

MITIGATING
- "We’re applying mitigation for <Component> in <Region>. Error rates are beginning to improve, but some impact may persist while changes roll out."

MONITORING
- "Mitigation is in place for <Component> in <Region>. We’re monitoring recovery and will confirm once we’re confident the service is stable."

RESOLVED
- "This incident has been resolved for <Component> in <Region>. If you continue to see issues, please contact Support with timestamps and request IDs."

Optional detail snippets (include only when true)
- Fallback/partial restore:
  - "We’ve enabled fallback routing to reduce impact." (Avoid naming the fallback model/region unless already publicly documented and non-sensitive.)
- Scope refinement:
  - "Impact appears limited to a subset of traffic." / "Impact is limited to streaming responses." (Only if we can defend the statement.)
- Customer action:
  - "No customer action is required." (Only if truly none.)

What NOT to say (public status updates)
- Do not mention: specific customers, tenant names, contract tiers, reserved capacity gaps, exact GPU counts, internal hostnames/services.
- Do not claim: "SLA breach" / "credits will be issued" (Support handles separately).
- Do not commit to exact ETAs unless approved by IC + SRE and high confidence.

Console linking copy (Console surfaces)
Goal: in-product status should help customers quickly find the public incident thread + post-incident summary, without duplicating too much detail (and without diverging from the Status Page).

Surface A: Global banner (top of Console)
Banner title options:
1) "Incident affecting <Component> in <Region>"
2) "Service disruption: <Component> (<Region>)"

Banner body (single sentence)
- "We’re currently investigating an issue affecting <Component> in <Region>. View live updates on our Status Page."

Primary CTA button
- "View status updates"

Secondary link (optional)
- "Contact Support"

Footer timestamp (recommended)
- "Last updated: <timestamp>"

Surface B: Inline banner on impacted pages (route-aware)
Example copy:
- Title: "Embeddings disruption in EU Central"
- Body: "Some embedding requests may fail or time out. For live updates, see the Status Page incident."
- CTA: "Open incident"

Surface C: Incident list view (Console → Reliability/Status)
List item fields:
- Title (same as Status Page incident title)
- Status pill: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved
- Impacted components + regions (chips)
- Last update time

Empty state copy
- "No active incidents. See our Status Page for historical incidents and post-incident summaries."

Resolved incident detail view (Console)
Top summary (2–3 lines max; keep aligned with the public post-incident summary)
- "On <date>, <Component> in <Region> experienced <issue type>, leading to <customer impact sentence>. The incident was mitigated and service returned to normal at <time>."

CTA links
- "Read the post-incident summary" (only once published)
- "View incident timeline" (links to status page incident)

Post-incident summary teaser (if available)
- Header: "What happened"
- Body: "We’ve published a summary covering impact, mitigation, and follow-up actions."
- CTA: "Read summary"

If summary is not yet published
- "A post-incident summary will be published after review." (No commitment on exact timeline unless policy states one.)

Dedicated / Private sensitivity notes (needs final sign-off)
We need consistent behavior across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Proposed rule (draft):
- Hosted incidents: always public status page + Console banner + Console link.
- Dedicated incidents:
  - If it affects the Dedicated control plane broadly (multi-tenant control plane issue), we can publish a public incident under "Dedicated Control Plane" component.
  - If it affects single-customer dedicated capacity or customer-managed configuration, do NOT publish publicly. Console should show a generic support guidance banner for that customer only (non-public).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): do NOT publish to public status page unless it impacts shared Redwood-managed services used by multiple customers (rare). Provide customer-specific comms via Support/CS.

Copy constraints (Dedicated/Private)
- Avoid stating or implying: "dedicated cluster capacity" / "reservation shortfall" / "customer-specific saturation".
- If we show anything in Console for a single tenant, phrase it as:
  - "We’re investigating an issue affecting your deployment. Please contact Support for updates." (and keep it visible only to that tenant).

Legal / security notes (open items)
- Michael/Naomi: confirm whether “fallback routing” is safe to mention publicly in general terms.
- Confirm whether we can mention “regional failover” without implying data residency moves (for regulated customers).
- Confirm standard language for: "If you continue to see issues…" and what identifiers are safe to ask for (request IDs OK; avoid asking for prompts/user content).

Edge cases + guidance
1) Partial region impact
- Prefer explicit component+region rather than “Global”.
- If only one AZ within a region: still say region publicly; do not mention AZ.

2) Latency-only degradations
- Use “Degraded performance” and include a customer impact sentence:
  - "Requests may take longer than usual to complete." + optionally "Streaming may be slower to start."

3) Streaming-only issues
- Use "Streaming" component rather than "Hosted API" unless non-streaming is also impacted.

4) Incident scope changes
- When we narrow scope: say so explicitly.
  - "Update: Impact is limited to <Component> in <Region>; other components are operating normally."

5) Customer actions/workarounds
- Only include if broadly applicable and low-risk.
- Avoid “retry aggressively” phrasing (can amplify load). If needed:
  - "If possible, reduce retry concurrency and use exponential backoff." (Consider if too technical for public updates—maybe keep for support KB.)

Console ↔ Status Page linking mechanics (copy dependencies)
- We need consistent naming between:
  - Status page component display names
  - Console banner/component chips
  - Incident-bot structured fields
- Copy assumes the incident object has: component(s), region(s), and a stable public URL.

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm the final region display names (US East vs us-east vs N. Virginia). We need one public string.
- Decide whether Console should show “Historical incidents” within the Console or link out only.
- Confirm the post-incident summary publishing policy language (“after review” vs “within X business days”). Waiting on PM-612 final.
- Confirm approval flow wording for Sev0/Sev1: do we say “Next update in 30 minutes” by default?

Change log (informal)
- 2025-11-15: Added Dedicated/Private sensitivity section after Console linking discussion w/ Marissa + Kira.
- 2025-11-18: Updated banner CTA to "View status updates"; removed “ETA” language.
- 2025-11-21: Added latency-only guidance + scope refinement update snippet.
